summary: This component builds an interactive project scaffolding tool that displays files and folders, lets users view them with syntax highlighting, copy a bash script to recreate the folder structure locally, or download everything as a ZIP file. It parses child components (file snippets, guidelines, empty folders) into organized lists and generates both a shell script and a downloadable archive from that data.

explanations.22: Object.assign attaches a marker property `isGuideline: true` to a component that renders nothing, so we can identify Guideline components later even after they're wrapped by other React elements.
explanations.28: Similar to Guideline, this creates a marker component for empty directories that need to exist but have no files.
explanations.47:
This walks through nested React elements (which might be wrapped in `

` tags from MDX) and extracts the plain text inside them.
explanations.86: This ref stores a timer ID so we can clear it later; useRef persists across renders without causing re-renders like useState would.
explanations.88: The cleanup function runs when the component unmounts to clear any pending timeout, preventing a memory leak or state update on an unmounted component.
explanations.95: useMemo caches the parsed file list, guidelines, and folders array so they're only recalculated when the `files` or `children` props actually change, not on every render.
explanations.113: We cast child.type to an object shape because TypeScript doesn't know custom components can have attached properties like `isGuideline`.
explanations.119: We check both if the component is literally the imported Guideline component AND if it has the isGuideline property, since MDX might wrap it.
explanations.130: We determine if a child is meant to be a file by checking if it's a Snippet component, has a filename/title prop, or is a custom component (not a plain HTML string like 'div').
explanations.158: In bash double quotes, `~` won't expand to the home directory, so we replace it with `$HOME` to ensure paths work correctly in the generated script.
explanations.172: This uses a heredoc (`cat <<'DELIMITER'`) to write file content safely; the single quotes prevent shell variable expansion, and the delimiter ensures multiline content works.
explanations.187: useCallback memoizes this function so it doesn't get recreated on every render; it's passed to event handlers and we only want it to update when shellScript changes.
explanations.194: useCallback async creates the ZIP; we wrap the logic in try/finally to ensure setIsDownloading(false) always runs even if something fails.
explanations.209: We strip leading slashes from the folder name because ZIP paths shouldn't start with `/`, which could cause issues or confusing nested structures.
explanations.214: JSZip.folder() returns null only for invalid folder names; we already sanitized, but we throw explicitly so the error handler below can catch and display it.
explanations.232: generateAsync with type 'blob' creates a downloadable binary object in memory; we can't use 'string' for binary ZIP data.
explanations.238: Some browsers (especially Firefox) won't trigger the download unless the link is in the DOM before we click it, so we append it temporarily.
explanations.344: We map fileList and conditionally render: if the file came from an originalNode (a Snippet component), we clone it with updated props; otherwise we render a basic Snippet.
